works.title: The Queen's Comic Ballet
works.company: court of Henri III / Louise de Lorraine
works.premise: The enchantress Circe is overcome by the gods and the king, restoring harmony to a realm torn by religious war.

works.title: Royal Ballet of the Night
works.premise: Twelve hours of night, with its thieves, witches and dreams, end as the young king rises as the Sun.

works.title: The Bourgeois Gentleman
works.premise: A social climber is tricked by a mock 'Turkish ceremony' into believing he has been made a mamamouchi.

works.title: Pygmalion
designer: Marie Sallé (costume reform - loose hair, muslin dress)
works.premise: A sculptor's statue comes to life; Sallé danced it uncorseted, a reform of costume and expression.

works.title: The Amorous Indies
works.premise: Love in four 'Indies' (Turkey, Peru, Persia, the American forest) as seen from the Opéra.

works.title: Don Juan
works.orig: Don Juan, ou le Festin de pierre
works.premise: The seducer is dragged to hell by the statue of the man he killed: a pantomime ballet that tells a whole tragedy without words.

works.title: Medea and Jason
works.company: court of Duke Carl Eugen of Württemberg
works.premise: Medea's revenge as a ballet d'action: the passions told in pantomime, the program of the Lettres sur la danse put on stage.

works.title: The Wayward Daughter
works.orig: La Fille mal gardée (Le Ballet de la paille)
works.premise: A farmer's daughter outwits her mother to marry the young farmer she loves rather than the rich simpleton.

works.title: Flore and Zephyr
works.premise: The west wind courts Flora; flying machinery lifts dancers into the air, a precursor of the Romantic illusion of weightlessness.

works.title: The Creatures of Prometheus
works.premise: Prometheus brings two statues to life and has them taught the arts, a parable of education and enlightenment.

works.title: Robert the Devil: Ballet of the Nuns
works.orig: Robert le diable: Ballet des nonnes
works.premise: Dead nuns rise by moonlight in a ruined cloister to seduce the hero: the scene from which the white act grew.

works.title: La Sylphide
works.premise: A Scottish farmer leaves his bride for an air spirit and destroys her by trying to possess her.

works.title: La Sylphide (Bournonville)
works.premise: The Paris ballet re-made in Copenhagen with a new score; the version that survived in continuous performance.

works.title: Giselle
works.premise: A village girl dies of a nobleman's betrayal and, among the vengeful ghosts of jilted brides, saves him.

works.title: Napoli, or The Fisherman and His Bride
works.orig: Napoli, eller Fiskeren og hans Brud
works.premise: A Neapolitan fisherman rescues his bride from a sea-god's grotto; the last act is a wedding tarantella.

works.title: La Esmeralda
works.premise: A Romani street dancer is loved by a priest, a poet, a captain and the bell-ringer, and condemned as a witch.

works.title: Pas de Quatre
works.premise: Four rival ballerinas share one stage, each given a solo to her strength; the star system made into a ballet.

works.title: Paquita
works.premise: A Romani girl in Spain saves a French officer and turns out to be of noble birth.

works.title: The Corsair
works.premise: A pirate rescues a Greek girl from a slave market and a pasha's harem; a shipwreck ends it.

works.title: The Butterfly
works.premise: A girl turned into a butterfly by a fairy is caught and pinned by the prince who loves her.

works.title: The Pharaoh's Daughter
works.premise: An English lord, dreaming in a pyramid under opium, lives a romance with a mummy who comes to life.

works.title: Don Quixote
works.premise: In a Barcelona square the knight blesses the love of an innkeeper's daughter and a barber, against her father's choice.

works.title: Coppélia
works.orig: Coppélia, ou la Fille aux yeux d'émail
works.premise: A village girl impersonates a toymaker's doll to win back her fiancé, who has fallen for the doll.

works.title: Sylvia
works.orig: Sylvia, ou la Nymphe de Diane
works.premise: A huntress-nymph of Diana is won by a shepherd with the help of Eros.

works.title: La Bayadère
works.premise: A temple dancer loved by a warrior is killed by his royal bride; in an opium vision he finds her among the Shades.

works.title: Swan Lake
works.place: Moscow, Bolshoi Theatre; St Petersburg, Mariinsky Theatre
composer: Pyotr Ilyich Tchaikovsky (1895 revised by Riccardo Drigo)
works.premise: A prince swears love to a woman turned into a swan and is tricked into betraying her by her black double.

works.title: Excelsior
works.premise: Light defeats Obscurantism through the inventions of the century, in a spectacle of hundreds of dancers.

works.title: The Sleeping Beauty
works.premise: A princess cursed by a slighted fairy sleeps a hundred years until a prince's kiss; a homage to the court of Louis XIV.

works.title: The Nutcracker
works.premise: On Christmas Eve a girl's nutcracker doll becomes a prince who takes her to the Kingdom of Sweets.

works.title: Raymonda
works.premise: A Hungarian-Provençal noblewoman waits for her crusader knight and resists a Saracen knight who tries to abduct her.

works.title: The Dying Swan
works.place: St Petersburg (charity concert, Hall of Nobility) (probable)
works.premise: A two-minute solo: a swan's last struggle; Pavlova's signature.

works.title: Les Sylphides (Chopiniana)
works.date: 1907/1908 (St Petersburg, as Chopiniana); 1909-06-02 (Paris, Théâtre du Châtelet, as Les Sylphides)
works.premise: A poet among sylphs in moonlight: a white act without a plot, a ballet about the Romantic ballet.

works.title: The Pavilion of Armida
works.premise: A traveller sleeps in a pavilion where a tapestry of Armida comes alive; awake, he finds her scarf.

works.title: The Firebird
works.premise: Prince Ivan captures the magic Firebird, spares her for a feather, and with her help destroys the immortal Kashchei.

works.title: Scheherazade
works.premise: While the shah is away his wives and the Golden Slave hold an orgy; he returns and has them killed.

works.title: Petrushka
works.premise: At a Shrovetide fair, a puppet with a soul loves a ballerina doll and is killed by the Moor; his ghost mocks the showman.

works.title: The Spirit of the Rose
composer: Carl Maria von Weber (Invitation to the Dance
works.premise: A girl home from her first ball dreams the rose she wore dances with her, then leaps out of the window.

works.title: Afternoon of a Faun
works.premise: A faun pursues nymphs in a flat frieze of profile movement and is left with a scarf.

works.title: Games
works.premise: A young man and two women look for a lost tennis ball in a park at dusk and trade kisses.

works.title: The Rite of Spring
works.orig: Le Sacre du printemps / Весна священная
works.premise: Pagan tribes celebrate spring; a chosen maiden dances herself to death.

works.title: Parade
works.premise: Fairground managers and acts try to lure a crowd into a show that never begins.

works.title: Autumn Leaves
works.premise: A chrysanthemum is torn by the autumn wind and abandoned by a passing poet.

works.title: The Magic Toyshop
works.premise: Two dancing dolls in a toyshop, sold to separate buyers, elope overnight with the other toys' help.

works.title: The Three-Cornered Hat
works.orig: Le Tricorne / El sombrero de tres picos
works.premise: A miller and his wife outwit a lecherous magistrate in an Andalusian village.

works.title: The Wedding Party on the Eiffel Tower
works.orig: Les Mariés de la tour Eiffel
works.premise: A wedding party on the Eiffel Tower is spoken by two phonograph-narrators while a camera swallows and spits out characters.

works.title: Skating Rink
works.premise: On a working-class skating rink, a madman steals a woman from her partner as the crowd circles.

works.title: The Triadic Ballet
works.company: Oskar Schlemmer with Albert Burger and Elsa Hötzel
works.premise: Three dancers in eighteen sculptural costumes move through yellow, pink and black sequences: the body as geometry.

works.title: The Creation of the World
works.premise: African deities create plants, animals and the first couple, in a European fantasy of Africa built from jazz and sculpture.

works.title: The Wedding
works.premise: A Russian peasant wedding as an impersonal rite: braiding, blessing, feast and bedding, with the couple as functions of the group.

works.title: The House Party
works.premise: A hostess, flappers, three athletes and an ambiguous 'girl in blue' flirt in a white salon: gender and desire in code.

works.title: Cancelled
designer: Francis Picabia (wall of car headlamps); René Clair (film Entr'acte)
works.premise: An 'instantaneist' anti-ballet: headlights blind the audience, a woman dresses and undresses, a film interrupts.

works.title: The Blue Train
works.premise: Bathers, a tennis champion and a golfer flirt on a Riviera beach: an operetta danced in real sportswear.

works.title: The Steel Step
works.premise: From the black-market Russia of the NEP to a factory where workers become parts of the machine.

works.title: The Red Poppy
works.premise: A Chinese dancer in a port city gives her life to save a Soviet ship's captain from her Western-backed lover.

works.title: Apollo
works.place: Washington, Library of Congress; Paris, Théâtre Sarah-Bernhardt
works.premise: The young god Apollo is born, taught by three Muses, chooses Terpsichore and ascends Parnassus.

works.title: Bolero
works.premise: A woman dancing on a tavern table draws the men around her into a rising frenzy.

works.title: Prodigal Son
works.premise: A son leaves home, is stripped by a siren and her thugs, and crawls back to his father's arms.

works.title: The Golden Age
works.place: Leningrad, State Academic Theatre of Opera and Ballet (Mariinsky)
works.premise: A Soviet football team at an industrial exhibition in a Western city is framed by fascists and freed by workers.

works.title: The Bolt
works.place: Leningrad, State Academic Theatre of Opera and Ballet
works.premise: A lazy worker throws a bolt into a machine to sabotage the factory and is caught by the Komsomol.

works.title: The Flames of Paris
works.place: Leningrad, State Academic Theatre of Opera and Ballet
works.premise: Marseille volunteers march on Paris and storm the Tuileries: the crowd as hero.

works.title: The Green Table
works.premise: Masked diplomats argue around a table, war breaks out, and Death collects everyone.

works.title: Destiny
works.premise: Man struggles with Fate across four movements: the earliest known 'symphonic ballet' set to a whole symphony.

works.title: The Fountain of Bakhchisarai
works.place: Leningrad, State Academic Theatre of Opera and Ballet
works.premise: A Crimean khan captures a Polish princess; his jealous favourite kills her and he builds a fountain of tears.

works.title: Serenade
works.date: 1934-06-10 (students, Woodlands estate, White Plains); 1935-03-01 (American Ballet, Adelphi Theatre, New York)
works.company: School of American Ballet / American Ballet
works.premise: Seventeen women in blue moonlight: a plotless ballet with a ghost of a story, made on students.

works.title: The Bright Stream
works.premise: City artists visit a kolkhoz harvest festival; cross-dressed disguises expose a philandering dacha-owner.

works.title: Icarus
works.premise: Icarus fixes on wings, flies and falls, danced to percussion composed after the choreography.

works.title: The Rake's Progress
works.premise: A young heir squanders his inheritance in Georgian London and ends in Bedlam.

works.title: Lilac Garden
works.premise: At a garden party before her arranged wedding, a woman tries to say goodbye to the man she loves.

works.title: Checkmate
works.premise: The Black Queen seduces and kills the Red Knight and corners the old Red King.

works.title: The Skaters
works.premise: Couples skate on a frozen pond at night; a show-off spins until the curtain falls on him.

works.title: Billy the Kid
works.premise: The pioneer march west frames the short violent life of the outlaw Billy.

works.title: Romeo and Juliet
works.place: Brno, Mahen Theatre; Leningrad, Kirov Theatre
works.premise: Two young lovers from feuding families of Verona die for a love their city cannot allow.

works.title: Laurencia
works.premise: Spanish villagers, roused by a woman assaulted by the Commander, rise and kill him.

works.title: The Colonel's Wife
works.place: Mexico City, Palacio de Bellas Artes
works.premise: Four episodes from Posada's Mexico: the young ladies of the old regime, the dance of the dispossessed, Don Ferruco's nightmare, the Last Judgement.

works.title: The Maiden Tower
works.place: Baku, Azerbaijan State Academic Opera and Ballet Theatre
works.premise: A princess throws herself from Baku's Maiden Tower rather than submit to a forced marriage.

works.title: Gayane
works.premise: On an Armenian collective farm, a woman exposes her husband as a traitor and saboteur.

works.title: Pillar of Fire
works.premise: A repressed woman, afraid of spinsterhood, gives herself to a stranger and is redeemed by love.

works.title: Rodeo
works.orig: Rodeo, or The Courting at Burnt Ranch
works.premise: A tomboy cowgirl tries to outride the cowhands and wins the Champion Roper by putting on a dress (or by not quite).

works.title: Fancy Free
works.premise: Three sailors on shore leave compete for two girls in a Manhattan bar.

works.title: Cinderella
works.premise: A mistreated stepdaughter goes to the ball with a fairy's help and is found again by a slipper.

works.title: Giselle (Alicia Alonso)
works.premise: A Cuban ballerina and company claim the Romantic classic as a national work and return it to Paris.

works.title: Shurale
works.date: 1945 (Kazan, Tatar Opera and Ballet); 1950-05-28 (Leningrad, Kirov, Yakobson)
works.company: Tatar State Opera and Ballet; Kirov Ballet
works.premise: A hunter steals the wings of a bird-maiden in a forest ruled by the wood-goblin Shurale and must defend her.

works.title: The Four Temperaments
works.place: New York, Central High School of Needle Trades
works.premise: Theme and four variations on the humours, danced in a new angular vocabulary; later stripped to practice clothes.

works.title: The Young Man and Death
works.orig: Le Jeune Homme et la mort
composer: J. S. Bach (Passacaglia in C minor
works.premise: A painter in a Paris garret is driven by a woman to hang himself; she returns as Death and leads him over the roofs.

works.title: Symphonic Variations
works.premise: Six dancers who never leave the stage against a pale green backcloth: postwar renewal as pure dance.

works.title: Symphony in C
works.orig: Le Palais de cristal / Symphony in C
works.premise: Four movements, four ballerinas, four colours of jewels (1947), merged into a finale of fifty dancers.

works.title: Etudes
designer: contested: Harald Lander (Bolshoi notes) or Rolf Gerard with lighting by Nananne Porcher (Wikipedia; probably ABT 1961 credits)
works.premise: A ballet class becomes the performance: from the five positions at the barre to a finale of massed leaps.

works.title: Fall River Legend
works.premise: A New England spinster, crushed by her stepmother and her town, takes an axe to her parents and goes to the gallows.

works.title: Carmen
works.company: Ballets de Paris de Roland Petit
works.premise: Carmen as a cropped-haired femme fatale in a stylised Spain: sex and death in forty minutes.

works.title: Miss Julie
works.premise: On Midsummer Eve a count's daughter seduces her father's valet and, shamed, takes his razor.

works.title: The Cage
composer: Igor Stravinsky (Concerto in D for strings)
works.premise: A tribe of female insects initiate a novice, who kills her male lovers.

works.title: Estancia
works.premise: A city boy wins a ranch girl by proving himself as a gaucho, ending in a malambo.

works.title: Afternoon of a Faun (Robbins)
works.premise: Two dancers in a studio meet in the mirror (the audience) and part after a kiss.

works.title: The Stone Flower
works.premise: A Ural stonecutter seeks to carve a perfect stone flower and is held by the Mistress of the Copper Mountain.

works.title: The White-Haired Girl (Matsuyama Ballet)
works.place: Tokyo, Hibiya Public Hall (日比谷公会堂)
works.premise: A peasant girl sold to a landlord flees to the mountains, her hair turns white, and the revolutionary army rescues her.

works.title: Agon
works.premise: Twelve dancers in practice clothes play out the combinations of twelve-tone music and old court dances as a contest.

works.title: The Fish Beauty
works.company: Beijing Dance School (北京舞蹈学校), choreography training class
works.premise: A fish-spirit falls in love with a young hunter and must resist the Mountain Demon to become human.
works.lane: Asia, Africa and the Middle East

works.title: The Rite of Spring (Béjart)
works.premise: The Rite as a mass mating ritual of a male and a female tribe, not a sacrifice.

works.title: La Fille mal gardée (Ashton)
works.premise: Lise and Colas outwit Widow Simone and the dim Alain, with a clog dance, a maypole and a ribbon cat's cradle.

works.title: Revelations
works.premise: From sorrow to baptism to Sunday celebration: African American spirituals in three sections.

works.title: Boléro (Béjart)
works.premise: A single dancer on a red table, the 'Melody', draws a circle of men, the 'Rhythm', into a crescendo.

works.title: The Legend of Love
works.premise: A queen gives up her beauty to save her sister; both love the painter Ferhad, who is set to cut a mountain to bring water.

works.title: The Red Detachment of Women
works.company: Central Opera and Dance Drama Theatre ballet troupe (now National Ballet of China)
works.premise: A slave girl on Hainan escapes, joins an all-women Red Army company and grows from revenge to class consciousness.

works.title: The Dream
works.premise: Oberon and Titania quarrel; Puck's love-juice muddles four lovers and gives Titania an ass for a lover.

works.title: At the Fountain
works.premise: A day at a village fountain: girls gossip, a troupe of travelling acrobats and Karagöz and Hacivat perform, night falls.
works.lane: Asia, Africa and the Middle East

works.title: Onegin
works.premise: A bookish girl's love is rejected by a bored aristocrat; years later, married, she rejects him.

works.title: Romeo and Juliet (MacMillan)
works.premise: The Prokofiev ballet re-made as gritty Renaissance street life around two teenagers.

works.title: Song of the Earth
works.premise: A man, a woman and a masked Messenger of Death pass through six songs on the transience of life.

works.title: The White-Haired Girl (Shanghai)
works.company: Shanghai Dance School (上海市舞蹈学校)
works.premise: Xi'er's story as a revolutionary model ballet: the landlord's victim becomes a fighter when the Eighth Route Army comes.
works.lane: Asia, Africa and the Middle East

works.title: Carmen Suite
works.premise: Carmen in a bullring of chairs, watched by spectators: fate, freedom and the corrida in one act.

works.title: Jewels
works.place: New York, New York State Theater
works.premise: Three plotless acts as three gems and three national styles of ballet.

works.title: Raka
works.company: PACT Ballet (Performing Arts Council of the Transvaal)
works.premise: A half-human creature, Raka, enters a village; only the warrior Koki resists him while the others are seduced.
works.lane: Asia, Africa and the Middle East

works.title: Spartacus
works.premise: The slave revolt of 73-71 BCE told through four characters: Spartacus, Phrygia, Crassus, Aegina.

works.title: Dances at a Gathering
works.place: New York, New York State Theater
works.premise: Ten dancers in a sunlit field meet, part and look at the sky, an hour of Chopin without a story.

works.title: The Ecstasy of Rita Joe
works.premise: A young First Nations woman who moves to the city is crushed by poverty, the courts and violence.

works.title: Anna Karenina
works.premise: A married woman's passion for an officer ends under a train.

works.title: Afternoon Siesta
works.premise: Four sisters in a colonial Cuban house dream of love and loss through an afternoon of Lecuona.

works.title: Manon
composer: Jules Massenet (arr. Leighton Lucas; not from the opera)
works.premise: A convent-bound girl chooses between a poor student and a rich protector, and dies deported in a Louisiana swamp.

works.title: The Rite of Spring (Bausch)
works.premise: On a stage covered in earth, the group chooses a woman by a red dress and she dances to death.

works.title: Push Comes to Shove
works.premise: Baryshnikov with a bowler hat leads a classical corps through Haydn, mixing ballet with shrugs, slouches and showbiz.

works.title: The Lady of the Camellias
works.premise: A Paris courtesan gives up her young lover at his father's demand and dies of consumption.

works.title: Mayerling
works.premise: A drug-addled, syphilitic crown prince, trapped by court politics, kills his teenage mistress and himself.

works.title: Rama, Hari
works.place: Manila, Cultural Center of the Philippines
works.premise: Prince Rama and Sita, exiled on the eve of his coronation, win back the kingdom, as a Filipino rock opera-ballet with singers among dancers.

works.title: The New Year's Sacrifice
works.company: Central Ballet of China (中央芭蕾舞团)
works.premise: Xianglin's widow, sold into a second marriage, loses husband and child and is cast out as unlucky by her village.
works.lane: Asia, Africa and the Middle East

works.title: Giselle (Mats Ek)
works.premise: The village outsider is driven mad by a man of another class; Act II is a psychiatric asylum.

works.title: Creole Giselle
works.premise: Giselle transposed to Louisiana's free Black society, where class is counted in generations from slavery.

works.title: In the Upper Room
works.premise: Dancers in sneakers and dancers on pointe emerge from fog in relays until everyone is exhausted.

works.title: Shim Chung
choreographer: additional choreography - Roy Tobias, Oleg Vinogradov, Bingxian Liu
works.premise: A daughter sells herself as a sacrifice to the sea to restore her blind father's sight, and returns from the Sea King's palace as a queen.
works.lane: Asia, Africa and the Middle East

works.title: The Kabuki
works.place: Tokyo, Tokyo Bunka Kaikan (東京文化会館)
works.premise: A young man of today falls into the world of Chūshingura and leads the 47 masterless samurai to revenge and ritual suicide.

works.title: In the Middle, Somewhat Elevated
works.premise: Nine dancers in practice clothes stretch classical positions to breaking point under hard light and industrial sound.

works.title: Swan Lake (Mats Ek)
works.premise: A prince's failed break from his mother; bald swans of both sexes.

works.title: The Hard Nut
works.place: Brussels, Théâtre Royal de la Monnaie
works.premise: The Nutcracker in a 1970s suburban party, with cross-cast roles and snowflakes of both sexes throwing snow.

works.title: The Park
works.premise: Four gardeners in dark glasses steer a man and a woman through a formal garden of love, from first glance to a flying kiss.

works.title: Swan Lake (Matthew Bourne)
works.premise: A modern prince starved of his mother's love meets a male Swan who embodies the freedom he cannot have.

works.title: Rites
works.company: Bangarra Dance Theatre with The Australian Ballet
works.premise: The Rite as the elemental forces of an ancient Australian landscape, danced by Indigenous and classical dancers together.
works.lane: Asia, Africa and the Middle East

works.title: The Grand Night
works.premise: A night at a village moulid: vendors, fortune-teller, circus, a lost child; puppets turned into dancers.

works.title: Raise the Red Lantern
works.company: National Ballet of China (中央芭蕾舞团)
works.premise: In a 1920s mansion, a new concubine loves a Peking-opera actor; the jealous second wife betrays them and all three are executed.

works.title: Chroma
composer: Jack White III (arr. Talbot; orch. Christopher Austin)
works.premise: Ten dancers in pale slips burst through one opening in a white architectural box to orchestral White Stripes songs.

works.title: Swan Lake (Dada Masilo)
composer: Arvo Pärt (probable for the last two)
works.premise: Odette is married off to Siegfried, who loves a male Odile; a requiem for those lost to AIDS and homophobia.

works.title: Alice's Adventures in Wonderland
works.company: Royal Ballet (co-production National Ballet of Canada)
works.premise: Alice follows a rabbit into Wonderland, where Victorian garden-party guests become cards, caterpillars and queens.

works.title: The Winter's Tale
works.company: Royal Ballet (co-production National Ballet of Canada)
works.premise: A king's jealousy destroys his wife and son; sixteen years later the lost daughter returns and the queen's statue comes to life.

works.title: The Sleeping Beauty (Ratmansky)
works.place: Costa Mesa, Segerstrom Center for the Arts
works.company: American Ballet Theatre (co-production Teatro alla Scala)
works.premise: The 1890 ballet recovered from notation: remaking by subtraction of a century's habits.

works.title: Woolf Works
works.premise: Three acts, three Woolf novels: memory, time travelling through bodies, and the sea of her death.

works.title: Giselle (Akram Khan)
works.premise: Giselle among migrant garment workers locked out of a closed factory; the Wilis are the ghosts of dead workers.

works.title: Jane Eyre
works.premise: An orphan governess falls in love with her employer and discovers the wife hidden in his attic.

works.premise: Fifty-four dancers with green-painted throats move as one living mass through the four seasons.

works.premise: Thirty-six dancers in grey coats move as one migrating mass, then a single parting at a door.

works.premise: A rough, violent Giselle in a South African village; the Wilis are ancestral spirits, and there is no forgiveness.

works.title: Cleopatra
works.premise: Egypt's last queen, her love for Antony, war, defeat and death, told by an Egyptian composer for Cairo's company.

works.title: Frida
works.place: Amsterdam, Dutch National Opera and Ballet
works.premise: Frida Kahlo's injured body, marriage and painting as a sequence of living pictures.

works.title: The Cellist
works.premise: A cellist's love affair with her instrument (danced by a man) and her loss of it to multiple sclerosis.

works.place: touring with Pina Bausch's Rite of Spring (Dakar / Europe) (probable)
works.company: Pina Bausch Foundation, École des Sables, Sadler's Wells

works.title: Like Water for Chocolate
